tool_schemas.name: execute_ssh_command
tool_schemas.description: Executes the provided shell command on the specified remote host using the given SSH connection details and returns the execution record including stdout, stderr, and the process exit code. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/invalid (e.g., empty host/username/command, non-numeric or out-of-range port, or both/none of password and privateKey when credentials are required), and AUTHORIZATION_ERROR if the caller is not permitted to execute commands or the referenced credentials cannot be used by the caller. Raises RATE_LIMITED when execution limits are exceeded, NOT_FOUND when the target host/profile or referenced credential cannot be resolved, and SSH_CONNECTION_FAILED when the session cannot be established or the command cannot be executed.

tool_schemas.name: list_ssh_command_executions
tool_schemas.description: Lists stored SSH command execution records in reverse-chronological order. Supports filtering by connection/host/username/status and time range. Refuses invalid filters and enforces pagination limits.

connection_id.description: Filter to executions created for a specific saved connection profile id.

host.description: Filter to executions for an exact host value.

username.description: Filter to executions for an exact username value.

status.description: Filter to executions in the given lifecycle status.

requested_from.description: Only return executions with requested_at >= this timestamp (RFC3339).

requested_to.description: Only return executions with requested_at <= this timestamp (RFC3339).

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned from a previous call.

tool_schemas.name: get_ssh_command_execution
tool_schemas.description: Fetches a single SSH command execution record by id. Returns the stored stdout/stderr (possibly truncated) and lifecycle fields. Raises NOT_FOUND if the id does not exist.

tool_schemas.name: cancel_ssh_command_execution
tool_schemas.description: Requests cancellation of an SSH command execution. Transitions status from queued->cancelled or running->cancelled when allowed; refuses with INVALID_STATE if the execution is already terminal.

id.description: The ssh_command_executions primary key to cancel.

reason.description: Optional human-readable reason recorded as a sanitized error_message.

tool_schemas.name: list_ssh_targets
tool_schemas.description: Lists SSH targets (host/port policies) with optional filtering by status and host. Returns records including allowed_command_regex when set. Refuses invalid pagination parameters.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned from a previous call.

tool_schemas.name: upsert_ssh_target
tool_schemas.description: Creates a new SSH target policy or updates an existing one. Setting status drives the active<->disabled lifecycle transition; refuses invalid transitions and invalid regex syntax. Returns the persisted target record.

id.description: If provided, updates the existing target with this id; otherwise creates a new target.

host.description: DNS name or IP address of the SSH host.

allowed_command_regex.description: Optional regex that commands must match when executing against this target.

metadata.name: SSH Server
metadata.description: This backend stores SSH connection profiles (hosts/users/ports and credential references) and a durable audit log of SSH command executions. The main workflow is: a client submits an execute request, the system resolves credentials, runs the command on the remote host, stores stdout/stderr/exit code
